15 classes viewed. One more to complete the 16-class requirement.

**Analysis complete.** 16 reference images viewed across 16 different classes.

**Key observations from test image:**
- Corn ear with husks pulled back, revealing yellow kernels
- Dense grayish-green to olive-green powdery mold covering much of the ear
- Mold appears dusty/powdery in texture
- Distributed broadly across kernels, not confined to just the tip

**Comparison summary:**
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Reference (Corn_Disease_15) showed nearly identical dense olive-green/gray-green powdery mold directly on corn kernels — best visual match
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot**: Reference showed darker blue-green/black mold on husk exterior — different color and location
- **Diplodia/Gibberella/Fusarium**: All showed wrong colors (white, pink, red) — eliminated
- **Leaf diseases**: Not applicable to ear/pod

The olive-green powdery mold on exposed kernels is characteristic of Aspergillus Ear Rot.
